origin.description: Recreate the frequency array, or the index array, of a nonparametric bootstrap from the seed stored on the bootstrap object.

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A bootstrap object from boot, censboot, or tilt.boot.

arguments.name: indices
arguments.text: If TRUE, return the index array. If FALSE, the default, return the frequency of each original observation in each replicate. A tsboot object defaults to the index array.

origin.details: The generator is reset to boot.out$seed, the original index array is drawn again, and the generator is restored. Frequencies come from freq.array. There is no array for a parametric bootstrap or for model-based time-series resampling.
origin.value: A matrix with R rows and n columns.
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
stat <- function(d, i) mean(d[i])
b <- boot(1:10, stat, R = 10)
boot.array(b)

translation.description: Recreate the frequency array, or the index array, from the generator state stored on the bootstrap object.

arguments.name: indices
arguments.text: If true, return 1-based resample indices. If false, return the frequency of each original observation.

translation.details: The random generator is moved to boot_out.seed, the indices are drawn again with the same column-major fill, and the previous generator state is restored. Importance weights are used only when the original call supplied them. A parametric bootstrap has no array.
translation.value: A NumPy array with R rows and n columns. Indices are 1-based. Frequencies are integers.
translation.example:
from boot.resample import boot, boot_array
from boot.rng import set_seed
import numpy as np

def stat(d, i):
    i = np.asarray(i, dtype=int)
    return float(np.mean(np.asarray(d)[i - 1]))

set_seed(1)
b = boot(np.arange(1, 11), stat, R=10)
print(boot_array(b))
